blocks.text: Zscaler's role-based administration enables you to assign Authentication Service users or user groups with admin roles and permissions and control their level of access to the Zscaler Admin Console.

If your organization uses Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), administrator roles for Authentication Service are managed on a different Role Management page. To learn more, see About Role Management. Unified RBAC is a feature in limited availability. To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.

blocks.item: Super Admin: System role with full permissions. You can assign this role to other admins if required.
View Only Admin: System role view only permissions.
User Admin: System role with user management permission.
CXO Insight User: System role with CXO insight permission.

blocks.text: Ensure that you have added users and user groups to Authentication Service before assigning necessary admin roles.

For Authentication Service tenants who have migrated to the Zscaler Admin Console, you must have at least the View Only permission for the Users and User Groups modules to submit a Zscaler Support ticket in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Role management provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Assign users and user groups as admins to manage tasks in Authentication Service.
View all the configured admins, their access levels, and functional scope.

blocks.text: On the Roles page (Administration > Role Management > Authentication Service), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Select the columns to display in the table and click Apply.
View a list of roles configured for your organization. For each role, you can view:
Name: The name of the role.
Description: The description of the role, if available.
You cannot delete predefined roles, and you cannot edit the custom role that is assigned to you individually. To learn more, see Assigning Entitlements to Users and User Groups.
